q8_low_vram.label: 8-bit model · loaded one part at a time

sources.locked: ai-toolkit ui/src/app/jobs/new/options.tsx (minimax_h3): the Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 repack (pruned int8 ConvRot transformer about 21 GB, nvfp4 Qwen3-VL-32B text encoder about 16 GB, about 43 GB with the video and audio VAEs), downloaded into the checkout's models folder on first load. H3 is guidance-distilled, so the recipe keeps ai-toolkit's default distillation handling: the ostris training adapter merged into the weights and contrastive guidance (do_guidance_loss, target 3.5), and the adaln_proj layers left out of the LoRA. Latents are cached. Motion mode reads the dataset as video: clips at 24 fps with auto_frame_count, so each clip trains at its own length snapped down to the video VAE's 17n + 5 frames (minimax_h3.py get_frame_count_snapper) and its sound stays in step (trim_auto_frame_count_tail, ai-toolkit's default); stills train beside them as single frames; no first-frame (i2v) conditioning
sources.divisibility: minimax_h3.py get_bucket_divisibility: 16 for the VAE x 2 for the patch size
sources.defaults: ai-toolkit UI defaults for minimax_h3 (timestep shift, adamw8bit, lr 1e-4, rank 16, do_audio on, audio_loss_multiplier 1). Training stays at 512: a 107-frame clip at 512 is 32 latent frames of 256 tokens each
sources.preview.base: minimax_h3.py model notes: guidance-distilled, keep guidance at 1; 28 steps at 24 fps. ai-toolkit previews 107 frames at 768, which ran out of memory on a 32 GB card with 30% of layers in RAM (an ai-toolkit run on the owner's machine); previews here are 56 frames (2.3 s) at 768, about 87 s each
sources.subject: heuristic, as for Z-Image Turbo: ai-toolkit's own caption dropout default is 0.0; content_or_style per jobs/process/BaseSDTrainProcess.py
sources.effort: ai-toolkit's MiniMax-H3 defaults (lr 1e-4, rank 16); the adapter's notes say it breaks down over long runs, so the step ranges stay under 3000. No source gives a steps-per-picture rule
sources.hardware_profiles: measured on an RTX 5090 (32 GB) with this recipe rendered by PixlStash: 6 updates at 512 on two 4.6 s clips with sound (trained as 107 frames) and two stills, rank 16, batch 1, a save and 56-frame 768 previews at 28 steps; the trainer's processes read every 0.25 s by nvidia-smi and their resident memory. vram_mb and ram_mb are the highest peak outside previews x1.1 (training/measurements.py NEED_MARGIN). About 6.8 s per update on a 107-frame clip. A longer clip trains more frames and needs more: nothing caps a clip's length
sources.hardware_profiles.q8_offload_60: measured: peaks 23.4 GB encoding captions, 21.8 GB training and previewing; 74.2 GB resident while the weights load, 43-56 GB after
sources.hardware_profiles.q8_low_vram.vram_mb: derived: without offloading the image recipe already ran out of memory on the 32 GB card loading the transformer; clips add about 5 GB of activations over stills at 1024
sources.hardware_profiles.*.ram_mb: measured, outside loading: the trainer's resident memory peaked at 55.7 GB after the weights were in, x1.1. While they load it reads 74.2 GB, but that includes the mapped weight files: both runs loaded with about 65 GB of RAM available, so the loading peak is left out of the seed
sources.hardware_profiles.*.max_rank, max_batch: rank 32 is derived from the rank 16 measurement (rank 16 LoRA state is about 0.2 GB); batch 1 as measured
